structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single reviewable CANDIDATE architecture/design document for Pre-Python configuration and installation at docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/configuration-and-installation.md, using named existing authority and evidence, without implementation, runtime changes, source/test/config edits, EOS edits, or approval of the architecture itself.
structuredContent.summary: The work packet has a clear documentation-only outcome, bounded artifact location, explicit source authorities, concrete acceptance topics, exclusions, and verification expectations. It authorizes drafting a candidate design that records unresolved Founder decisions rather than resolving them silently. Configuration, SecretProvider, installer/bootstrap, health, rollback/resume, transport selection, provider/work-management mapping, and upgrade safety are semantically coupled enough to be handled as one cohesive design artifact.
implementation_unknowns: Exact content and structure of the named local source materials must be inspected during implementation, including existing profile/config examples, operations documentation, authority sections, and historical bootstrap evidence.
The document author must determine the best traceability format for mapping each proposed contract/invariant to source authority and evidence.
The author must identify which design points are already founder-resolved versus which remain candidate material requiring later Founder approval.
The author must decide how to present successful and failing examples clearly without implying implementation API stability or adopted authority.
The author must ensure any references to candidate EOS source material are limited to conformance pin usage and not treated as blanket adoption.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through review of the produced markdown artifact and any local packet/readiness evidence: it should cover all listed design topics, label material architecture/security/storage semantics as CANDIDATE, include source/invariant mapping, examples, scope limitations, unresolved Founder decisions, and avoid prohibited implementation or operational changes. One independent content review can provide a meaningful verdict because the output is a single bounded document judged against supplied authority rows and source evidence rather than implementation correctness.
material_risks: The document could accidentally present candidate architecture as Founder-approved authority rather than reviewable design material.
The author could invent new decisions where the packet requires reuse of cited material and explicit recording of unresolved cross-document choices.
Traceability may be incomplete if source sections, invariants, and examples are not mapped concretely.
Scope could creep into implementation planning, source/config/test edits, service setup, secret handling, or live operational changes, all of which are excluded.

Configuration, SecretProvider, transport, provider routing, work-management mapping, and upgrade safety have security and compatibility implications that must be clearly marked as candidate where not already resolved.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed to draft the bounded candidate design document and local packet/readiness evidence only, using the named local baselines and authority materials, then submit it for independent content review against the stated acceptance criteria.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the owner intent is specific and bounded, the authorized scope is documentation-only, material exclusions are explicit, prerequisites are reported as existing local baselines, and unresolved architecture decisions are to be documented rather than decided silently. Remaining uncertainty is implementation research about reading and organizing source evidence, not a material owner question. The work is cohesive around configuration and installation design, and any likely rework is localized to the single candidate artifact.
